provider-truth.instructions: Start from providerContracts and the complete providerRegistry within the shard's declared scope; do not audit only the best-documented providers. For every claim, distinguish schema/registry presence, implemented adapter behavior, mocked safety and lifecycle coverage, current official provider documentation, and successful live-conformance evidence. Repository prose, implementation notes, metadata, and mocked tests are claims rather than independent proof. A ready-for-live or planned capability must not be described publicly as supported. A supported claim without concrete linked or committed live-conformance evidence from the last 90 days is a finding; never infer a live pass from test code. Verify provider API behavior only through current official documentation on the allowlisted hosts and include exact source URLs in evidence. If required official documentation cannot be reached, set complete=false and report the source gap. Compare the public website and docs with test/provider-conformance/provider-matrix.ts, providerRegistry metadata, adapter ports, focused tests, and live harness coverage. Report contradictions, missing lifecycle layers, stale evidence, undocumented limitations, and claims broader than the implemented or verified contract. Do not mutate resources, run opt-in live tests, use provider credentials, edit files, or promote statuses.

shards.instructions: Audit every hosting lifecycle and public support claim for Railway, Google Cloud Run, AWS ECS Express Mode, and Azure Container Apps. Cover project and service identity, deploy sources and managed CI recipes, runtime and environment wiring, maintenance, custom domains, teardown, mocked contracts, and recent live evidence. Include every registered capability owned by these hosting adapters, but do not audit data providers or integrations assigned to other shards.

Audit every hosting and edge lifecycle and public support claim for DigitalOcean App Platform, Vercel, Fly.io, Cloudflare DNS and load balancing, and GitHub Pages routing. Cover durable identity, deploy and runtime behavior, maintenance, certificates and domains, DNS ownership, teardown, mocked contracts, and recent live evidence. Do not audit code-host collaboration or integrations assigned to other shards.

Audit every registered database, cache, storage, queue, resilience, restore-drill, and data-migration capability and public claim. Include Railway data services, Cloud SQL and Google Cloud Storage, RDS, S3 and ElastiCache, Azure Blob Storage, Supabase, Neon, Fly Managed Postgres, and every other providerRegistry entry in this resource scope. Cover private creation, scoped identity, observation, runtime wiring, data-plane behavior, retry-safe teardown, mocked contracts, and recent live evidence.

Audit every registered email, messaging, payments, source-control and CI, AI, app-store, and secret-manager capability and public claim. Include SendGrid, Twilio, Stripe, GitHub and GitLab collaboration/CI excluding Pages routing, OpenAI, Apple, 1Password, Bitwarden, Doppler, Vault, and every other providerRegistry entry in this integration scope. Cover credential boundaries, provider behavior, lifecycle safety, mocked contracts, and recent live evidence.
